Query CrateDB as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__cratedb.R
oauth_db_cratedb_api.Rd

Query CrateDB data using the signed-in visitor's database privileges. CrateDB checks their access token and matches it to a database user. The client sends SQL over HTTPS and returns data frames.

Usage

oauth_db_cratedb_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  schema = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 300,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS SQL endpoint, including /_sql and any proxy prefix.

schema

Default schema, or NULL for CrateDB's doc default.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one HTTP operation.

ca_bundle

Optional trusted CA certificate bundle path.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A client object with these methods:

  • $query(sql, parameters = list(), raw = FALSE) returns a data frame, or the complete result with metadata when raw = TRUE.

  • $execute(sql, parameters = list()) runs a statement and invisibly returns its affected row count (-1 when unknown).

Details

Configure CrateDB's HTTP JWT authentication and a database user matching the token's iss, username and aud claims. The CrateDB vignette explains the provider requirements.

Create the client inside server() and call its methods from render or reactive expressions. Each request uses a current token and discards results after sign-out or account changes. SQL doesn't retry automatically. A submitted query can continue after a timeout; check a failed write's outcome before resubmitting it.

Parameters and results

Use $1, $2, ... or ? placeholders with an unnamed list of values in parameters. Values travel separately from SQL. Scalars, missing values, arrays and named-list objects are supported. Dates and timestamps become ISO strings; cast the placeholders to the SQL type you need. For exact large integers or decimals, use strings and SQL casts. Numeric parameters must be finite.

BIGINT and NUMERIC results stay as strings. Smaller numbers become R numeric values and booleans become logical. Dates and timestamps use epoch-millisecond strings; complex types use list columns with numbers preserved as strings. Empty results keep their column types.

raw = TRUE returns metadata and rows, with numeric row values kept as strings. HTTP errors report the status without exposing server messages or credentials.

See also

vignette("cratedb", package = "shinyOAuthDB"). oauth_db_demo() runs a local CrateDB and Keycloak example.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
crate <- oauth_db_cratedb_api(auth$connection,
  url = "https://crate.example.org:4200/_sql", schema = "doc")
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  crate$query("SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE country = $1 LIMIT 20",
    parameters = list("NL"))
})
} # }
